newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses stage recovery as Dow rallies.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses stage recovery as Dow rallies.

text.p: A firmer start on Wall Street on Tuesday reversed early losses on European stock exchanges that were digesting record highs hit by no fewer than eight bourses on Monday.

London, Europe's biggest exchange, closed at a record high on the back of Wall Street, where the Dow jumped the 6,000-point hurdle about an hour after its opening. It failed to sustain gains above that level, however, and was up about six points at 5,986 when the London market closed.
London rallied after an early dive when the government said shareholders would no longer be able to claim tax credits on share buybacks or special dividend payouts.
The surprise statement initially wiped almost 30 points off the blue chip FTSE 100 index. But it closed 4.1 points higher at 4035.6 -- its third consecutive record close.

Dealers said the initial reaction to the tax ruling had been overdone and was exaggerated by players trying to trigger a break downwards in a market some believed had gone too far, too fast in recent weeks.

They said that although the timing of the British Treasury's announcement had been a surprise, its content was not. They noted that companies would still continue to generate cash and find alternative ways to funnel funds to shareholders.

The news came one day before shareholders at the international news and information group Reuters Holdings Plc were due to vote on a 613 million pound ($957.6 million) share buyback scheme. The company promptly put its plans on hold.
Reuters shares came under pressure following the government's announcement, dropping to a low of 750 pence before closing at 757, down 20 pence.
In Frankfurt, German shares ended floor trading weaker, before Wall Street opened, but post-bourse electronic trading reversed most of the losses.

Shares in sportswear maker Adidas jumped on news it will be an official sponsor for the 1998 soccer world cup. They rose to a record high of 145 marks before ending the bourse session in Frankfurt up 1.40 marks at 143.40 marks.
The Paris bourse also turned positive on the back of Wall Street in the afternoon and closed up almost half a percentage point.
Shares in debt-mired Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA fell after they were requoted following a week's suspension, amid disappointment over the terms of its restructuring with creditor banks.
The shares closed at 8.35 francs. They were 9.15 francs when they were suspended on September 30.

Among other European bourses, Dutch and Swiss shares closed at record highs, though only marginally up from Monday. On the currency markets, dealers said the dollar was stumped for inspiration in late European trade.
It was undermined by a firming mark -- boosted when a Bundesbank council member urged clear, credible fulfilment of the European monetary union convergence criteria.
Franz-Christoph Zeitler's call echoed Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer's warning on Monday that countries should not "window dress" economic data in order to meet EMU requirements.
But the dollar shrugged off French prime minister Alain Juppe's assertion that it was chronically undervalued.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5268 marks and 111.22 yen compared with 1.5299 marks and 111.22 yen late in Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKET -- CLOSING PRICES
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 4.1 points higher at 4,035.6.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 9.99 at 2,161.54.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 11.47 at 2,691.17.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $381.00 compared with $380.15 at the London close on Monday. Silver closed unchanged at $4.90.
